text:
Marathon Petroleum rose 1.66% today, extending a sharp two-week rally of 22.6%. The move reflects an escalation in Middle Eastern tensions: Iran attacked Saudi Aramco facilities and a container ship in the Strait of Hormuz, raising concerns about crude oil supply disruptions. With global oil prices climbing to $125 per barrel (versus $96 domestically), refiners like Marathon benefit from wider profit margins on the fuel they produce and sell.

The broader tailwind is a diesel shortage expected to persist into 2027 due to the Iran conflict, falling inventories, and strong demand. Refineries are already running at 92.7% capacity, leaving little room to ramp up production—which means tight supply conditions and stronger pricing power for fuel producers over an extended period.
